title: A protocol to quantify chromatin compaction with confocal and super-resolution microscopy in cultured cells
protocol: Detach HeLa cells from maintenance cultures in T75 flasks or p10 dishes.
Discard the exhausted culture medium.
Seed HeLa cells in 8-well chambers.
Allow cells to attach for 24 hours before challenging them with drug treatments or other experimental conditions.
Wash cells gently with 5 mL of PBS, and discard.
Add 1 mL Trypsin-EDTA (0.25%), phenol red to each flask.
Incubate flasks for 3 min at 37°C in cell incubator.
Visually inspect the plate for complete cell detachment before proceeding.
Tap gently on the sides of the flask/dish to favor cell detachment.
Add 9 mL of complete culture medium and pipette gently up and down to disaggregate cells.
Collect detached cells in 15 mL Falcon tubes.
Count HeLa cells with a standard or automated cell counter.
Prepare a cell suspension to achieve 1 × 10^5 cells/mL.
Place the volume of cell suspension containing 800,000 cells in a 15 mL Falcon tube.
Dilute it with complete culture medium until reaching a total volume of 8 mL.
Seed 350 μL of HeLa cell suspension in 8-well chambers and return plates to the incubator for DAPI confocal imaging or H3K9me3 STORM imaging.
Add 4 μL of EdC 10 mM solution to the 8 mL of cells suspension for DNA STORM imaging (final concentration 5 μM).
Seed 350 μL of this suspension in 8-well chambers and return plates to the incubator.
Replace culture medium in all wells with 350 μL of pre-warmed resting medium after 24 h from seeding for DAPI confocal imaging or H3K9me3 STORM imaging.
Replace culture medium with 350 μL of pre-warmed resting medium plus EdC at a dilution of 1:2000 in wells designated to DNA STORM imaging.
Replace resting medium in all wells with 350 μL of fresh resting medium plus ActD at a final concentration of 5 μg/mL.
For DNA STORM imaging wells, also add EdC in a dilution of 1:2000.
Discard the medium after 5 hours of ActD incubation or corresponding alternative treatment.
Wash cells 3 times with PBS for 5 minutes each.
Fix cells with 300 μL of PFA 4% for 10 minutes at 20°C–25°C.
Wash cells 3 × 5 minutes with PBS.
Cover chamber lids with 400 μL PBS and seal plates with parafilm if storing fixed cells at 4°C for up to 1 month.
Inspect wells visually before resuming the protocol after storage.
Bring cells to 20°C–25°C before permeabilization.
Permeabilize cells with Triton 0.4% for 15 minutes.
Wash cells 3 × 5 minutes with PBS.
Proceed directly to Click Chemistry reaction step if performing DNA STORM imaging.
Incubate cells with Click Chemistry solution for 30 minutes, protecting from light.
Wash cells three times with PBS for 5 minutes each, protecting from light.
Store samples at 4°C until imaging or proceed directly with STORM imaging.
Proceed directly to immunostaining step if performing H3K9me3 and STORM imaging.
Incubate wells with blocking buffer for 1 hour at 20°C–25°C.
Incubate wells with Rabbit polyclonal anti-H3K9me3 diluted in blocking buffer 1:50 for 12–16 hours at 4°C.
Wash cells three times with washing buffer for 5 minutes each.
Incubate cells with 1:250 Goat anti-Rabbit IgG AF647 in blocking buffer for 1 hour at 20°C–25°C in the dark.
Wash secondary antibody with Washing buffer twice for 5 minutes each.
Wash once in PBS.
Proceed directly with STORM imaging or store at 4°C until imaging.
Incubate wells with Blocking buffer plus DAPI diluted 1:1000 in PBS (final concentration 1 μg/mL) for 15 minutes at 20°C–25°C in the dark.
Wash three times with PBS.
Pause stained cells for up to 2 days at 4°C in the dark, covered with PBS and sealed with parafilm.
Inspect wells visually before resuming protocol to ensure normal cellular morphology and absence of contamination.
Inspect cells for abnormalities in cell density and fluorescent signal before proceeding with imaging.
Set parameters of image acquisition for confocal microscopy: use an image size of 1024 × 1024, pinhole 1, scan speed 400 Hz, bidirectional scan, and a zoom of 1.
Adjust laser power and gain for the DAPI channel to satisfy dynamic range by imaging at least 10 fields per condition.
Visually inspect objective lens for proper state before use.
Place one drop of Type F oil in the center of the objective lens.
Mount the chamber on the stage-holder quickly but carefully.
Adjust the focus on the central stack of the cells.
Proceed with image acquisition.
Repeat the step for at least 9 other fields per condition.
Adjust laser power and gain to prevent DAPI signal saturation even in the brightest condition.
Visually inspect the objective for proper state.
Place one drop of Type F oil (Nikon) (RI 1.515) in the center of the objective lens.
Mount the chamber on the stage-holder quickly but carefully.
Replace PBS with freshly prepared STORM imaging buffer in the well to image.
Set camera to 17 MHz, EM Gain 100V and image size to 256 × 256 pixels.

Detect the AF647 fluorescence in the sample by using a laser compatible with AF647 fluorophore excitation (peak at 647 nm) and starting at a low power coupled with a 100 ms exposure, to avoid blinking and sample bleaching.
Adjust focus and illumination angle for optimal signal on the central stack of the cells.
Take a single snapshot of the nucleus/nuclei to be acquired.
Set the camera exposure time at 10 ms.
Increase the 647 nm laser power to approximately 2 kW/cm² to visualize single molecule blinking.
Launch image acquisition with simultaneous illumination of the sample using 647 nm and 405 nm lasers.
Use the 647 nm laser at a constant ∼2 kW/cm² power density.
Gradually increase the 405 nm laser power from 0.005 kW/cm² to 0.5 kW/cm² during imaging.
Acquire typically 60,000 frames per condition.
Image at least 10 fields per condition.
Generate localization lists from STORM images using Insight3 or Nikon NIS elements.
Perform drift correction with Insight3 by selecting “Save Molecule List” to generate a .bin file.
In NIS elements, go to Input & Output in the Molecule analysis section and select Export.
Choose “Export to BIN file (M425)” to generate .bin files.
Discard STORM imaging buffer every hour by aspiration with a pipette and replace it with freshly prepared buffer.
Replace STORM imaging buffer with PBS and store samples in the dark at 4°C when not performing imaging.
Create a folder containing .tiff files to be analyzed and the script FIJI_MACRO_CV.txt.
Open Fiji Is Just ImageJ software.
Load the .tiff files into ImageJ.
Import the FIJI_MACRO_CV.txt script.
Perform automated analysis using ImageJ for coefficient of variation measurement.
Save output files in the same folder as input files.
Include both the name of the source image and the index of the selected ROI in the output file names.
Open one single-channel .tiff image.
Run FIJI_MACRO_CV.txt from Plugins > Macros > Run….
Check generated masks if they correctly match single nuclei.
Visually inspect if masks generated are correct.
If masks are correct, close all files.
If masks are incorrect, change the minimum threshold value in FIJI_MACRO_CV.txt between 0 and 255.
Keep maximum intensity value at “255” to include broad range of intensity.
Save modified .txt.
Re-analyze images from step 14.
Modify the ROI analyzed if needed.
Adjust the "Watershed" command if required.
Discard incorrectly identified nuclei by eliminating corresponding .tiff files.
Run step 14 and step 15 for every image to be analyzed.
Open MatLab software.
Open MATLAB_CV_Confocal.m script.
Change the parameter categ with the number of experimental conditions.
Change the parameter Folder with the path of the data folder.
Load single nuclei .tiff files generated in step 15.
Open one window for each experimental category.
Click Done to proceed.
Two pop-up windows with graphic representations of results will appear.
Analyze the distribution of pixel intensities of single cells as shown in CV_Histplot_individualcells.
Plot the mean and standard deviation of the distribution of pixel intensities for each category as shown in CV_Histplot_smooth.
Write “Y” to visualize the boxplot of the CV calculated or “N” to skip visualization.
Open MatLab software.
Open Main code: “BlackSpace_MAIN” contained in Data S2.
Change the parameter "categ" with the number of experimental conditions.
Change the parameter "Directorio" with the path of the data folder given as a string.
Change the parameter "categname" with the names of the experimental categories given in cell format.
Check and adjust image dimensions by defining maxX and maxY values.
Define Gaussian sigma value (e.g., 2) for blurring images.
Adjust adaptive threshold value (e.g., 0.001) for DNA mask generation.
Load .bin files for each experimental category.
Click Run to process the images.
Save calculated results as a .xls file named "Blackspace_results.xlsx".
Load .bin files for each experimental category.
Two pop-up windows with graphic representations of the results will appear for each analyzed file.
Write “Y” (Yes) in the Command Window to visualize density renderings or “N” (No) to skip visualization and press Enter.
Calculated values are automatically saved in a file named ‘EDGE_analysis_results.xlsx’ in your specified folder.
